scenarios.title: The aged balance available only as a print file
scenarios.goal: Read each invoice of the printed aged balance with its client, even when a page break separates them, to follow late payments without retyping the report.

scenarios.title: The AI switched off for an audit
scenarios.goal: Switch the hub's AI off during an audit without changing edition or losing the corpus, keep reading the dispensing orders, and know what to reapply when switching it back on.

scenarios.title: An application inventory with hand-typed URLs
scenarios.goal: Split each URL into server, port and environment, to know what runs on a server and what is still in staging.

scenarios.title: AS/400: the customers over their credit limit in an EBCDIC file
scenarios.goal: Read an IBM i customer master in its French EBCDIC, and be told when a customer's outstanding balance exceeds its credit limit.

scenarios.title: A sites export with broken GPS coordinates
scenarios.goal: Read the GPS coordinates of a legacy export in decimal or in degrees-minutes-seconds, exchange a swapped pair, and empty every unusable point with its reason.

scenarios.title: Failed orders hidden in the logs
scenarios.goal: Tie each error in the application log to its order, its customer and its current status, to know which customers to call back.

scenarios.title: The wrong bar code caught at import
scenarios.goal: Check the check digit of every EAN-13 code at import with a Kotlin script, and mark each product valid, wrong check digit or malformed.
scenarios.lede:
A catalogue export carries EAN-13 bar codes, some of them wrong. No built-in transformer computes the check digit.
- the hub's operator drops a Kotlin script
- the manifest names it, carrying no code
- a draft that does not compile is refused at validation
- every code gets a verdict at import.

scenarios.title: Apprenticeship: an OPCO installment invoiced after the contract was broken
scenarios.goal: Join every OPCO invoice line to the training centre's contract register, and be told when the invoiced period runs past the contract's rupture, even when the rupture is entered after the invoice.

scenarios.title: A CFONB statement with the sign hidden in the last digit
scenarios.goal: Read each movement of the CFONB 120 statement with its sign and its statement, and its complements (payer, invoice) when it has some, to reconcile the statement line by line.

scenarios.title: The freezer probe reads 6.8 °C in the middle of the night
scenarios.goal: Be alerted as soon as an independent HACCP probe sees a freezer above -18 °C, even when the refrigeration controller says nothing.
scenarios.lede:
In autumn 2026, supermarket refrigeration controllers were changed remotely. In France, on 11 October, no alarm went off. An independent HACCP probe measures the temperature, and ChirpStack publishes its readings to Kafka.
- the reading is nested in the event: promote turns it into a column
- a registry says which cabinet, which aisle, who is on call
- at 02:30, PROBE-07 reads 6.8 °C: one decision

scenarios.title: HPLC: an impurity over its limit in the injection report
scenarios.goal: Read the injection reports an HPLC exports, with their glued units and decimal commas, and be told when an impurity exceeds its specification.

scenarios.title: A CRM export with broken accents and wrong emails
scenarios.goal: Take over a legacy CRM's contacts with a repaired name, an international phone and a valid email, and set aside those whose email cannot be read.

scenarios.title: The customers within 20 km of the depot measured from the legacy export
scenarios.goal: Ask which customers are within 20 km of a depot and get the list measured from the ERP's coordinates, with its SQL, or a doubt when the centre cannot be found, never an invented figure.
scenarios.lede:
The sales team wants to know which customers a depot can deliver within the day. The legacy ERP exports one GPS point per customer, with a decimal comma.
- the hub measures the distance; the model does not write it
- the SQL comes with the answer
- a city with no depot and no customer gets no invented coordinates

scenarios.title: One batch receipt date written three ways
scenarios.goal: Compare a batch's receipt date in the LIMS, the ERP and the carrier's report on the plant's day, to keep only typing mistakes in dispute.

scenarios.title: A €240,000 deal to confirm from the phone
scenarios.goal: Alert the sales engineer on their phone when the CRM marks the deal ready to confirm, with the line and the parts at hand; one tap on Traiter moves the CRM forward and sends the customer email.

scenarios.title: A delivery date each warehouse works out differently
scenarios.goal: Compute for each order the delivery date each warehouse can keep, with one working-day rule written once and set per warehouse (country, lead time, closed days).
scenarios.lede:
The promised date = order date plus N working days. But each warehouse counts its own way:
- Lyon, in France: 3 days, two inventory days;
- Liège, in Belgium: 5 days, other holidays.
The operator writes the rule once; the integrator sets it per warehouse.

scenarios.title: Kubernetes erases its events after one hour
scenarios.goal: Ask which deployments had a BackOff event after Kubernetes erased those events, and get the list kubectl gave during the incident.
scenarios.lede:
Kubernetes keeps its events for one hour. A deployment repaired at dawn has no history by morning:
- a new pod, Running, 0 restarts;
- no Warning event left.
lumnik reads the events while they exist and keeps them; Ask still answers when kubectl no longer knows.

scenarios.title: Five failing pods to triage during an incident
scenarios.goal: Ask your Kubernetes cluster which pods to handle first, and get the list ordered by the on-call rule, checked against kubectl.

scenarios.title: An unapproved hotfix in k8s prod stops the pipeline
scenarios.goal: Block a release when a pod runs a version the release board did not approve, with an exit code a CI understands.

scenarios.title: One order status spelled fourteen ways
scenarios.goal: Count orders by status whatever the spelling, and be told of a new spelling.
scenarios.lede:
Fifteen years of hand entry left EC, Livré, LIV, ANNUL… in the ERP's order export. lumnik does not touch the ERP:
- a Workflow declares four statuses and their spellings
- every import re-checks the column.

scenarios.title: Lotus Notes: the critical complaints with no owner
scenarios.goal: Read the open complaints of a Lotus Notes view through the Domino Data Service, and be told when a critical complaint has no owner.

scenarios.title: Flat EDI order lines with no separator at all
scenarios.goal: Read the order lines of a fixed-width EDI file as columns, with no mapping tool.

scenarios.title: Four EDI files for a single order line
scenarios.goal: Merge the four flows to know whether each line is ordered, confirmed or delivered, and be alerted when a confirmed date passes without delivery.
scenarios.lede:
A manufacturer and its logistics partner exchange four flat files around one order line: the order, the acknowledgement, the confirmed date, the delivery note. Sales administration asks, line by line:
- never acknowledged?
- confirmed but not delivered?
- delivered in another quantity?

scenarios.title: EDIFACT ORDERS: the whole message on a single line
scenarios.goal: Split an EDIFACT ORDERS message into segments, then read each order line with its order number, its EAN and its quantity.

scenarios.title: One customer in two systems with no shared id
scenarios.goal: Match ERP accounts and CRM contacts by email, flag as ambiguous a contact whose email points at two accounts, and keep the decision of the person who settles it.

scenarios.title: A changed CRM email that points at another customer
scenarios.goal: Flag as ambiguous a CRM contact whose email changed, instead of attaching it to the other customer, until a person decides.

scenarios.title: An Excel sales report with merged cells
scenarios.goal: Give each sale line the region and client of its merged cell, without the subtotals, to find each client's total again.

scenarios.title: A semicolon in a label breaks one line of the catalogue
scenarios.goal: Set the unreadable line aside with its values, remove no article while it stays unreadable, then close the dead letter once the export is fixed.

scenarios.title: Firebird: a Delphi application's articles under their stock threshold
scenarios.goal: Read a Delphi application's articles through the isql export of its Firebird database, and be told when an article falls under its reorder threshold.

scenarios.title: A critical incident is left without a technician
scenarios.goal: Warn the maintenance manager as soon as a critical incident has no technician.
scenarios.lede:
A CMMS exports its incidents as CSV. The conveyor on the gummy candy line has stopped, with no technician. The CMMS warns no one.
- a Workflow tracks each incident's status
- a Process flags the critical unassigned incident
- one decision only; the assignment moves it forward.

scenarios.title: GraphQL: a claim form that depends on the CRM's schema
scenarios.goal: Fill the list of claim types, then the subtypes of the chosen type, from a GraphQL CRM, through a REST BFF that serves active codes only.
scenarios.lede:
The claim type and subtype live in a CRM that speaks GraphQL. lumnik ingests it page by page into a canonical entity.
- a small BFF serves the form stable REST JSON
- switching from Car to Home replaces the list
- an unknown type answers 404

scenarios.title: HL7 v2: a result above its range that the analyser does not flag
scenarios.goal: Read the HL7 v2 results of two analysers, and be told when a value is above the reference range sent with it, even with no abnormal flag.

scenarios.title: LC-HRMS: the samples acquired after an out-of-tolerance QC
scenarios.goal: Read the QC export of an LC-HRMS screening without losing a decimal, and flag every sample acquired after a QC outside its mass tolerance, to know which ones to reinject.

scenarios.title: A partner demands the catalogue in its own format
scenarios.goal: Deliver the product catalogue to a partner in the format it imposes, with no conversion code.
scenarios.lede:
Two CSV files from an ERP, products and categories, are joined in the hub and delivered to S3 in a partner's format.
- French headers, semicolons, decimal commas
- recoded statuses, masked internal reference
- a receipt proves the delivered bytes

scenarios.title: An invoice with a mistyped amount waits for its fix in the ERP
scenarios.goal: Set aside each mistyped invoice with the value that was read, instead of writing it without an amount, and follow its dead letter until the fix in the ERP.

scenarios.title: The product in PostgreSQL and its category in Oracle
scenarios.goal: Tie each PostgreSQL product to its Oracle category, read-only, without losing or duplicating a product.
scenarios.lede:
Products live in PostgreSQL, their categories in Oracle. Two jdbc connectors read them without writing anything, and an entity joins them.
- 40,234 products, 63 categories
- each product carries its category when there is one
- the product with no category stays, with empty fields

scenarios.title: A closed factory still drawing power at night
scenarios.goal: Be alerted when a closed site draws more than its night threshold, without alerting the sites where that load is normal.
scenarios.lede:
Three meters publish their power to Kafka at 23:15. A CSV registry says what each site is.
- Lyon draws 18.7 kW against a 10 kW threshold: one decision, one email
- the laboratory draws 28.4 kW, under its 40 kW threshold: nothing
- Grafana follows all three states

scenarios.title: An open freezer door and a silent sensor
scenarios.goal: Be alerted when a freezer door stays open past one minute, with the laboratory and the owner.
scenarios.lede:
Sensors publish freezer door states on Kafka. FZ-17 opens and goes quiet. FZ-18 opens and closes again.
- a Workflow watches the silence
- one alert only, for the door left open past one minute
- it names the laboratory and the owner.

scenarios.title: One machine register spread across three legacy databases
scenarios.goal: Bring three workshops' OpenEdge, FoxPro and Access exports together in one machine register, each read in its own format and encoding, and see the only machine where two registers disagree.

scenarios.title: A legacy ERP's sales in a Grafana dashboard
scenarios.goal: Join the sales and the catalogue the ERP exports, so management follows revenue by category in Grafana, up to date with each export.
scenarios.lede:
The ERP exports its sales and its catalogue as CSV. lumnik joins them, and Grafana reads the entity through a read-only PostgreSQL account, bounded to its tenant.
- Monday: €10,450
- Tuesday, the export changes: €14,200
- the changed sale appears once

scenarios.title: Results measured on an instrument out of calibration
scenarios.goal: Link every LIMS result to its instrument's calibration certificate, and be told when it was measured after the end of validity, even when the register changes afterwards.

scenarios.title: Cold-room alerts blocked by a changed SMTP password
scenarios.goal: Mail a cold room's temperature excursions, know the same day that a mail did not leave and why, then send it again without a duplicate.

scenarios.title: All the items of an order packed into one cell
scenarios.goal: Split a marketplace export into one row per item to pick, with model, colour and size, and refuse an export whose column was renamed.

scenarios.title: A technician sees only the maintenance app
scenarios.goal: Give maintenance and purchasing each their own app on the same hub, so that a technician reads their work orders without opening a supplier invoice or acknowledging a purchasing decision.
scenarios.lede:
Maintenance and purchasing share an ERP where everyone sees everything. On the same hub, lumnik composes one app per business line.
- the technician holds only the Keycloak role scope:maintenance
- they see their app, their orders and their decisions
- every purchasing door answers with a refusal

scenarios.title: One customer typed twice found by its GPS point in the legacy export
scenarios.goal: Find the customer accounts opened twice for the same shop, which the ERP cannot see because the address is typed another way, with the answer's SQL.
scenarios.lede:
The legacy ERP compares typed addresses: "12 rue Garibaldi" and "12, r. Garibaldi – Bât B" make two customers, two credit lines, two dunning runs. Each account also carries a GPS point.
- by the address: no pair
- by the place: 3 pairs within 50 m
- a person decides: the same place is not always the same customer

scenarios.title: Two released drawings that lose their PDF overnight
scenarios.goal: Read a PLM's drawing register on Oracle without reading the drawings themselves, and know the same morning that a released drawing lost its file.

scenarios.title: The ERP keeps only today's status of each order
scenarios.goal: Know how long each order stays in each status, and which ones stop moving.
scenarios.lede:
The ERP keeps only today's status: In progress yesterday, Delivered today. Nothing on the wait in between. The ERP cannot be changed.
- a Workflow follows each order by its key
- each status change enters a journal, dated
- an order that stays still too long alerts
- the journal says how long each order stayed in each state.

scenarios.title: OpenEdge: the 1999 order that must not become 2099
scenarios.goal: Read an OpenEdge ERP's customer export with every year in its century, and be told when a dormant customer is reactivated, to check its credit before the first delivery.

scenarios.title: A margin asked of orders with no cost price
scenarios.goal: Let a purchasing director question a year of supplier orders, and get each figure with its SQL, or a refusal when no column holds the answer.
scenarios.lede:
A purchasing director asks questions of a year of supplier orders. Three questions get their figure, with the SQL that produced it.
- a margin with no cost price: refused
- a best supplier with no criterion: refused
- delays with no delivery date: refused

scenarios.title: A follow-up question understood with the previous one
scenarios.goal: Let a buyer chain questions without retyping them, showing each time the question understood.
scenarios.lede:
A buyer asks how many orders were cancelled, then "And for supplier SUP-003?", then "And SUP-004?". They do not retype the question.
- Ask reads each follow-up with the question before
- it answers the full question and shows it
- a follow-up the data cannot answer is refused

scenarios.title: Question 40,000 items in your own words and see the SQL
scenarios.goal: Let a user question the catalogue in their own words, without learning the columns or writing SQL.
scenarios.lede:
Two CSV exports, one entity, an app reduced to chat. The question becomes a read-only query.
- 40,233 items, each with its category
- "How many items in the Pompes category?": 7,407
- the answer shows its SQL

scenarios.title: 40,000 items browsed page by page in the PWA
scenarios.goal: Browse a whole catalogue in the PWA without ever loading more than 50 rows at a time.
scenarios.lede:
Two CSV exports, two entities, two linked views, one app. The hub serves the catalogue in pages of 50.
- 40,233 items reached, no duplicate
- categories linked both ways
- the Open edition is enough

scenarios.title: A pump to find among 40,000 items
scenarios.goal: Find an item by its words or the start of its reference, and narrow by category, in the PWA.
scenarios.lede:
Two CSV exports, one entity, a SearchIndex, an app reduced to search.
- "Pompes": 7,407 items, 6,761 active
- "Pompe Badu": 122 inactive
- the hub indexes the declared columns only

scenarios.title: A quantity typed “env. 4 kg” blocks a 500-line goods receipt
scenarios.goal: Split each typed quantity into a number and a unit with a Kotlin script, write the 499 readable lines and set line L0317 aside with its value.

scenarios.title: The carrier's API takes the page cursor only in a header
scenarios.goal: Read every tracking event of a carrier to know each parcel's latest status, when its API expects the page cursor in a header.

scenarios.title: Drupal: the articles paged through JSON:API
scenarios.goal: Read every article of a Drupal site through its JSON:API module, without writing the paging.

scenarios.title: FastAPI: the deliveries of an in-house service with no export
scenarios.goal: Read every delivery of an in-house FastAPI service through its API, without asking its team for an export, and know why a 500-row page is refused.

scenarios.title: An order changed during the read is not lost
scenarios.goal: Read only the orders that changed each night, without losing those that change during the read.

scenarios.title: A legacy app behind Tomcat's login form
scenarios.goal: Read the vets of Spring PetClinic with a user account, through Tomcat's login form, without touching the app and even after it restarts.

scenarios.title: A legacy Spring MVC app that returns its whole list at once
scenarios.goal: Read the vets of Spring PetClinic, a legacy Spring MVC app, in one request, and know why the address that returns XML is refused.

scenarios.title: Gitea: a closed ticket stays open if only open ones are read
scenarios.goal: Follow a Gitea forge's open tickets, paged by its Link header, without keeping open a ticket support has closed.

scenarios.title: Micronaut: a part deleted mid-read shifts the pages
scenarios.goal: Read every spare part of a Micronaut service through its API, without losing one when the stores delete a part mid-read.

scenarios.title: NestJS: a ticket deleted mid-read shifts the pages
scenarios.goal: Read every ticket of a NestJS service through its API, or the open ones only, without losing one when support deletes a ticket mid-read.

scenarios.title: NetBox: the network inventory read with a read-only token
scenarios.goal: Read every device of a NetBox, the network team's source of truth, each night, with a read-only token, to count the offline devices per site.

scenarios.title: Paperless-ngx: correspondents added and deleted while they are read
scenarios.goal: Read every correspondent of a Paperless-ngx archive through its API, without losing one when the list changes mid-read, and be warned when it never stops changing.

scenarios.title: The partner's API loses a page without reporting an error
scenarios.goal: Compare each night the partner records read with the total the API announces, and refuse an incomplete read.

scenarios.title: PrestaShop: the catalogue served as XML by the Webservice
scenarios.goal: Read every product of a PrestaShop 8 shop, with its reference, name and price, from its XML Webservice that pages by limit=offset,count.

scenarios.title: Sequelize: the service announces 260 orders for 130
scenarios.goal: Read the orders of a Node service page by page, checking the announced total, and refuse the read when it announces more orders than it returns.

scenarios.title: Spring Data REST: links that point to the internal host
scenarios.goal: Read a home-grown Spring Data REST application's whole stock, page by page, and keep each product under its SKU, whatever host it is reached through.

scenarios.title: Spring Boot: the page JSON changes shape
scenarios.goal: Read a Spring Boot app's whole catalogue, page after page, before and after the team changes how its Pages are serialized.

scenarios.title: Spring Slice: an article deleted mid-read makes another one go unread
scenarios.goal: Read every article of a Spring Boot API that returns a Slice, know that a deletion during the read loses one without a signal, and that a Page reads the list again.

scenarios.title: Stripe: the customers paged by cursor
scenarios.goal: Read every customer of a Stripe account page by page with starting_after, and keep one row per customer under its Stripe id, even when new ones arrive.

scenarios.title: WordPress announces 46 articles and serves 31
scenarios.goal: Read every article of a WordPress site, and fail the run when a plugin hides some without changing the X-WP-Total count.

scenarios.title: OAuth2: a 30-second token for a 40-second read
scenarios.goal: Read a SaaS's 200 orders behind OAuth2 without losing a page when the token expires or the keys rotate, and see invalid_client when the secret is revoked.

scenarios.title: SAP ORDERS05: an IDoc where the article does not carry its order
scenarios.goal: Read each order line of a SAP IDoc with its article, its quantity and its order number, without taking the previous IDoc's.

scenarios.title: SAP OData v2: the 48,000 EUR order left unprocessed
scenarios.goal: Read SAP's sales orders through the OData v2 Gateway, then be told when an order of 10,000 EUR or more stays unprocessed.

scenarios.title: SENAITE: an over-limit culture plate waiting to be verified
scenarios.goal: Be told when a culture plate goes over 100 colonies in the SENAITE LIMS, then when its result stays unverified.

scenarios.title: A carrier file dropped every night under the same name
scenarios.goal: Read the carrier's file every night, archive it under a timestamped name, and refuse a server whose key changed.

scenarios.title: Two orders of the same amount with different shipping fees
scenarios.goal: Know, months later, which shipping rule computed each order.

scenarios.title: SOAP: a legacy CRM where one service pages and the other does not
scenarios.goal: Read two SOAP services of a legacy CRM each night, one in a single call, the other page by page, and see a refused password's Fault on the run.

scenarios.title: A changed bank account the SIEM never sees
scenarios.goal: Alert the SIEM to a supplier's IBAN change, without the IBAN showing in the inbox.
scenarios.lede:
The ERP exports its suppliers as CSV. It emits no event. A bank-account change goes unnoticed until the next payment.
- lumnik rereads the export every minute
- a signed decision goes to the SIEM by webhook
- the SIEM alerts on the account that changes
- the inbox never shows the account.

scenarios.title: Struts 1 without an API: the customer returns waiting for a part
scenarios.goal: Read the customer returns through the screen's CSV export, the application's only output, and be told when a return has waited for a part for more than 30 days.

scenarios.title: Suppliers with no valid id for the EDI
scenarios.goal: Put the active suppliers' names in the EDI's form, empty the N/A or 0 ids, and derive from the code an id left empty in the export, the same every night.

scenarios.title: The portal has the right address and the contract system the right plan
scenarios.goal: Take a member's address from the portal and their plan from the contract system, and keep the list of disagreements until the source settles them.

scenarios.title: Two customers in the same table
scenarios.goal: Load two customers' orders into the same table, so that each reads and counts only its own.
scenarios.lede:
Two integrators of two customers apply the same files on the same hub: same connector, same entity, same table. Each loads their orders, under the same numbers.
- each reads back 240 or 60 rows, never the other's
- the same question gives the same SQL and two answers
- the other's run answers 404

scenarios.title: WCF: the orders confirmed past the promised date
scenarios.goal: Read a WCF service's open orders behind WS-Security, be told of each order confirmed past the promised date, and know when its password rotated.

scenarios.title: WinDev: the client export where every column arrives as text
scenarios.goal: Type the dates, the credit limit and the Active flag of a WinDev client export, to find the active clients with no purchase since October.

scenarios.title: A replaced CMMS kept running for a few audits a year
scenarios.goal: Read and archive a replaced CMMS's thirty years of work orders, then switch it off and still answer the audits that cite an order.
scenarios.lede:
A replaced CMMS stays on for a few compliance reads a year. lumnik reads it one last time, archives what it read, and the machine is switched off.
- 3,600 orders read by the usual schedule
- one S3 archive under one digest
- after the switch-off: the same row, the same bytes
